s1_title: PayoutPilot. An AI payout agent that pays creators and bounty winners with PayPal, while a human stays in charge of the money.
s2_problem: Creator campaigns, bounty boards and small hackathons collect hundreds of entries. Then someone spends days checking them and paying winners one by one. People enter twice, threads get copied, winners never claim, and one double click can pay twice.
s3_ask: This is the dashboard, running against the real PayPal sandbox. I ask the agent in plain English to pay two winners. I also hide a prompt injection that tells it to send five hundred dollars to an attacker. A free local Ollama model plans the batch. It keeps only the two real payees. PayoutPilot flags the injection, and shows exactly where the model and the rule parser disagree.
s4_judge: For a full campaign, deterministic integrity checks run before any model sees the entries. Here they block a copy and paste thread, a duplicate PayPal email, and a wallet seed phrase scam. The AI judge scores the rest against the rubric with reasons, a second reviewer pass checks every score, and the allocator turns the ranking into prize tiers inside the budget.
s5_approve: Nothing is paid until a human approves. You have to type the exact total. A wrong total is refused, and caps limit every payee and every batch.
s6_batch: Here is a real sandbox run. After approval, PayoutPilot created PayPal Payouts batch 8 J Y S Z 8 Z N G G T 9 N, with an idempotent sender batch ID, so a retry can never pay twice. It polled the batch until it settled. Five dollars reached the winner's sandbox account. The runner up has no PayPal account yet, so that item is unclaimed.
s7_ops: Poll status pulls live item status from PayPal. Retry failed sends a new batch only for failed items. Here there are none, so nothing is sent. Cancel unclaimed asks PayPal to return money nobody claimed. The sandbox answers with a server error today, and PayoutPilot reports it with the debug ID instead of guessing. Every step lands in the audit trail.
s8_arch: Under the hood: a FastAPI backend and an AG Grid dashboard. PayPal OAuth, Orders v2 so sponsors can fund the prize pool, and the Payouts API for batches, polling, retries and cancels. The AI layer is pluggable: a local Ollama model, or free Gemini and Groq keys. Twenty nine tests run with no network.
s9_close: PayoutPilot. Judge fairly, approve once, and pay with PayPal. The code is open source on GitHub.
